subtopics.content: i. Influence of Islam on the socio-political life of West African empires: Ghana, Mali, Songhai and Borno
subtopics.objective: Analyse the influence of Islam on the socio-political systems of selected West African states.

subtopics.content: ii. Impact of Islam on the economic life of West African states: Timbuktu, Kano and Borno
subtopics.objective: Evaluate the impact of Islam on the economic life of Timbuktu, Kano and Borno.

subtopics.content: i. Aims and objectives of Islamic education
subtopics.objective: Explain the aims and objectives of Islamic education.

subtopics.content: ii. The Glorious Qur’ān and Hadīth on education (Q.96:1-5; Q.39:9)
subtopics.objective: Assess the position of the Glorious Qur’ān and Hadīth in education.

subtopics.content: iii. Hadīth: “The search for knowledge is obligatory on every Muslim” (Ibn Majah)
subtopics.objective: Examine the importance of seeking knowledge in Islam.

subtopics.content: iv. Hadīth: “Seek knowledge from the cradle to the grave”
subtopics.objective: Examine the importance of seeking knowledge throughout life in Islam.

subtopics.content: v. Hadīth: “The words of wisdom are a lost property of the believer… a better right to it…” (Tirmidhi)
subtopics.objective: Examine the importance of wisdom and the pursuit of knowledge in Islam.

subtopics.content: vi. Intellectual activities of Islam in West Africa: development of written history in Arabic and establishment of Sankore University
subtopics.objective: Analyse the intellectual activities of Islam in West Africa.

subtopics.content: vii. Intellectual activities of Ahmad Baba of Timbuktu, Sheikh al-Maghili, Sheikh Usman Danfodio, Sultan Muhammad Bello and Ibn Battuta
subtopics.objective: Assess the contributions of Sheikh al-Maghili, Sheikh Uthman Dan Fodio, Sultan Muhammad Bello and Ibn Battuta to education.

subtopics.content: viii. Islamic educational institutions: House of Wisdom in Baghdad, al-Azhar University in Cairo and Nizamiyyah University in Baghdad
subtopics.objective: Account for the development of intellectual centres in Baghdad and Cairo.

subtopics.content: ix. Lives and contributions of Ibn Sina, Al-Ghazali, Ibn Rushd, ar-Razi and Ibn Khaldun to education
subtopics.objective: Examine the contributions of Ibn Sina to medicine; assess al-Ghazali’s contribution to Islamic education; analyse Ibn Rushd’s contribution to philosophy and fiqh; assess ar-Razi’s contribution to philosophy; and analyse Ibn Khaldun’s contribution to modern sociology and the method of writing history.
